Team Vingrohi

A team of passionate individuals trying to make resource management and survival on a Martian outpost more tangible, fun and accessible for young learners through our game.

Our team consists of five members,  Protyay serves as the Team Leader and Game Developer, working alongside Amit, who also contributes to game development. Ratul handles concept design and quality assurance, Habib is responsible for cinematography and Tithy takes care of research.
summary:
Planet Red is a first person perspective Mars survival and mission training game developed in Unity by Team Vingrohi for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It places players in the role of a junior astronaut exploring the challenges of surviving on Mars. Guided by an intelligent, stationary AI assistant named Beacon, players undertake missions involving essential aspects of Martian survival, including oxygen production, water resources, food cultivation, and habitat management.

Inspired by real NASA research and technologies, the game transforms complex scientific concepts into interactive, mission based experiences. Players learn about the challenges of establishing a sustainable human presence on Mars by completing objectives and interacting with scientifically inspired equipment, including a MOXIE inspired oxygen generation system.

Planet Red addresses the challenge by combining game based learning, exploration, and problem solving to create an accessible astronaut training experience, particularly for younger audiences. It is important because it makes space science more engaging and understandable while encouraging curiosity about planetary exploration, engineering, and the future of human exploration beyond Earth.
details:
Project Details

Planet Red is an interactive Mars survival and mission training game developed using Unity. It puts players in the role of a junior astronaut on Mars, where they explore a Martian environment, interact with different systems, and complete missions based on the challenges of establishing a sustainable human presence on the planet.

At the center of the experience is Beacon, a stationary AI assistant located near a damaged spacecraft. Beacon acts as the player's mission guide, introducing objectives, explaining scientific concepts, and assigning survival tasks. Through these missions, players explore important aspects of Martian survival, including oxygen generation, water resources, food production, and habitat development. The game also features Moxie2, a creative model inspired by NASA's Mars Oxygen In Situ Resource Utilization Experiment (MOXIE), representing the next generation of technology for producing oxygen from the Martian atmosphere.

The project aims to make space exploration and planetary science more accessible, particularly to younger audiences. Instead of simply presenting scientific information, Planet Red encourages players to understand these concepts through exploration, interaction, and problem solving. It provides an engaging introduction to the engineering and scientific challenges astronauts may face during future Mars missions.

The project was developed using the Unity game engine, with 3D environments, interactive models, game objects, and gameplay systems. Our team focused on creating an immersive Martian atmosphere while balancing scientific accuracy, educational value, and enjoyable gameplay.

What makes Planet Red creative is its approach to combining astronaut training with interactive storytelling and game based learning. We considered the target audience, scientific relevance, accessibility, gameplay experience, and the practical challenges of simulating a Martian settlement. Our intended impact is to inspire curiosity about space science and help the next generation better understand what it takes to explore and eventually live beyond Earth.
